title: Dominic and the Group Chat
premise: Wendell Vane has spent senior year invisible, raising her younger siblings while her mother works nights — until a forced semester project with her nemesis, Dominic Reyes, drags her into the orbit of his chaotic friend group and their group chat. The chat's real purpose emerges: the members are heirs to 'the Lantern Walk,' a town tradition about to be erased by a developer with the mayor's blessing. As Wendell digs into archives and old grievances, she discovers the tradition was built on an injustice that was never acknowledged — and that saving it honestly means exposing what her own family helped bury. In the end, Wendell chooses truth over safety: the walk is saved, reinvented with its full history told, and she graduates having traded invisibility for a found family that sees her completely.
about_author: Isandro Zhou is a former small-town newspaper reporter who writes young adult fiction about kids who fix what adults broke. They live in a river town much like the one in this book, where they still attend every lantern festival.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A day in her double life: packing lunches at 6 a.m., acing chemistry, dodging Dominic Reyes's smirk in third period. When the teacher announces semester project pairs — Vane and Reyes — her careful invisibility cracks. Emotional beat: resentment masking exhaustion; she refuses to let anyone see how tired she is.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Project meetings migrate to his kitchen table, where his friends — Priya, Marcus, and quiet Junie — treat Wendell like she belongs there. She gets added to the group chat against her will. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; their warmth feels like a trap or a door, and she can't tell which.

chapters.title: Group Chat Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via chat logs and scenes. Wendell learns the chat isn't just memes: it's the planning hub for the Lantern Walk, a century-old tradition the town council just voted to suspend for a riverside development. Dominic's grandmother founded the walk. Emotional beat: reluctant investment; Wendell starts researching for the project and can't stop.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Digging through the historical society's basement, she finds photos of the first Lantern Walk — and a name scratched out of every record: the family who donated the land, erased after a dispute. Her own great-grandfather signed the erasure order. Emotional beat: dread; the tradition she's fighting for was built on burying someone.

chapters.title: Nemesis Terms
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Wendell confronts Dominic privately; he already knows about the erased family — the Delgados — and admits the walk's founders stole credit for Junie's ancestors' idea. He's been sitting on it, afraid the truth will kill the tradition entirely. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition; two people who guard secrets recognize each other.

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Home life frays — a sibling's school crisis collides with a council meeting, and Wendell misses the vote on the development permit. Dominic covers for her without being asked. Emotional beat: guilt cracking open into trust; she realizes she doesn't have to carry everything alone, but letting go terrifies her.

chapters.title: The Developer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The developer turns out to be connected to the school — and starts pressuring students, offering scholarships for silence. Priya nearly takes the deal; the group chat fractures over tactics: petition, protest, or expose. Emotional beat: temptation and fracture; justice outside the law starts costing something real.

chapters.title: Junie Speaks
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The quietest member finally tells the full story her grandmother passed down — the Delgado lanterns were the original ones, lit first, named first. The group decides the walk can't be saved by hiding this. Emotional beat: reclamation; memory becomes evidence, and grief becomes fuel.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the eve of the final council hearing, the developer files to demolish early. The group scrambles — Wendell proposes the riskiest move: hold the walk anyway, illegally, on the disputed land, with the true history read aloud. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve; Wendell, the girl who stayed under the radar, plans the most visible act in town.

chapters.title: Lanterns, Lit First
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Hundreds come to the unsanctioned walk; the Delgado story is read from the courthouse steps, and the developer's permit collapses under public scrutiny. The council reinstates the tradition with the full history attached. Wendell's siblings watch her lead it. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; she graduates seen, held, and unafraid of the light.
